column1: # Witness-attested key of the ASF Mediceo del Principato 384 prefix-code cipher (Aug-Sept 1547).
# Built strictly from the three bilingual/deciphered witnesses in the same filza:
#   - c. 76r / c. 79r (French ambassador at Rome, 10 Aug 1547; extending Brice Dudout's frozen key_76r.tsv across L01-L18)
#   - c. 77r top cipher / bottom cleartext (Giovan Battista Ricasoli, Bishop of Cortona, 23 Sept 1547)
#   - c. 147r / c. 148r ("Adviso di Roma da persona degna di fede", on Bernardino Maffeo & Fieschi)
# ZERO values in this file are derived from target c. 78r (catalogue 2339).
# Target-inferred homophones and contextual hypotheses on c. 78r are kept strictly separate in key_78r_extensions.tsv.
# Prefix-code rule: plain 6, 8, 9 are 1-digit vowels (e, o, a); digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 start 2-digit codes.
# Diacritic override: a 2-digit group marked with an overbar (e.g. 68̄, 85̄, 55̄) or a dot on a 6/8/9 lead digit
# (6^7 = Signor, 8^9 = Vescovo, 9^3 = Ambasciatore) forms a 2-digit nomenclator code overriding the 1-digit vowel rule.
